hook: This 100% Natural Blend Supports The Health Of Your Ears And A Quiet Mind
claim: Quietum Plus is one of the best-known 'ear health' supplements, sold to support hearing and a 'quiet mind' for people bothered by ringing in the ears.
story: Its ingredients are a male-libido formula: mucuna, maca, epimedium (horny goat weed), tribulus, muira puama, catuaba, damiana, L-arginine and L-tyrosine, plus ashwagandha, ginger, piperine and vitamins. None is a recognized hearing ingredient.
ing_note: The label also lists vitamins A and B. Amounts aren't disclosed. Several of the cited references are animal or computer-modeling studies (for example tribulus in mice and ginger in a computational drug-design study).
price_note: Quietum Plus is sold as 2 bottles (+$9.99 shipping), 2+1 bottles or 3+3 bottles with free shipping; the order page shows crossed-out totals ($358, $1,074) with the actual price at checkout.
checks: None of the ingredients has clinical evidence for hearing or tinnitus.
Most are traditional aphrodisiacs; the formula appears designed for men's libido.
Mucuna contains L-dopa, which interacts with antidepressants and blood pressure medicines.
The seller warns that restocking 'can take up to 9 months', a common pressure tactic.
cons: Libido formula sold for ear health
verdict: Quietum Plus doesn't contain anything that supports hearing. If you have tinnitus or hearing loss, see an audiologist; hearing aids, sound therapy and tinnitus-focused CBT have real evidence. People on antidepressants, Parkinson's or blood pressure medicines should avoid mucuna-based products.
